MANAGEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY REPORT 2024


<!-- página 2 -->

Presentation
Banco de Occidente is a corporation with securities in
the market through the trading system of the Colombian
Stock Exchange for ordinary and subordinated bonds. As
of December 31, 2024, $4.00T has been issued and $3.90T
has been placed, of which $3.90T of series A Fixed Rate
and B under IBR are still in force, with average opening
and maturity terms being 2016 and 2028, respectively.
At the end of 2024, the current issuance and placement
program is $12.00T with an available limit of $6.00T to
meet the needs of raising resources.


Likewise, Banco de Occidente’s shares are registered
and traded on the Colombian Stock Exchange under the
modality of ordinary shares.


 City of principal domicile:
 Santiago de Cali, Valle del Cauca, Colombia
 Address of the main address:
 Carrera 4 # 7-61.

<!-- página 9 -->

Presentation
               SDG 13.1; 17.5
               I GRI 2-5 I

               We are pleased to present Banco de Occidente’s Management and Sustainability Report, reflecting
               our commitment to transparency, accountability and responsible management in the environmental,
               social and governance fields. This report summarizes the actions carried out by our bank in the
               period between January 1 and December 31, 2024 and has been prepared in reference to the
               Essential option of the GRI (Global Reporting Initiative) Standards and in compliance with Circular
               031 of 2021 of the Finance Superintendence of Colombia.
               In its development, we identify the most relevant aspects of our sustainable management, highlighting
               the achievements reached and the goals that we continue to promote. As part of our commitment
               to transparency and continuous improvement, we have included the GRI Content Index, as well as
               the Sustainability Accounting Standards Board (SASB) sector indicators for the commercial banking
               industry. We also adopted the recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial
               Disclosures (TCFD), strengthening our climate disclosure strategy.
               To guarantee the quality and reliability of the information presented, this report has been submitted
               to an Independent Limited Assurance process by the firm BDO Audit S.A.S. Regarding financial
               information, we have the tax audit of KPMG S.A.S. This external verification reaffirms our commitment
               to integrity, alignment with regulatory frameworks, and the adoption of international best practices.
               The report also accounts for our contribution to sustainability at a global level, evidencing our
               voluntary management around the ten principles of the Global Compact and our participation in key
               initiatives such as the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the Dow Jones Sustainability Index
               (DJSI), the United Nations Environment Programme – Finance Initiative (UNEPFI), among others.
               To facilitate the understanding of our contribution and compliance with these standards, we
               have included graphic references throughout the report, such as [GRI 2-25], [SASB FN-CB-
               410a.2] and the iconography of the SDGs, which allow us to clearly identify our commitment.

 In this way, the results presented allow us to maintain the profitability indicators within the
 Bank’s expectations. Thus, the Annual Return on Total Assets in December 2024 was 0.73%
 and the Annual Return on Equity was 9.33%.
 At the consolidated results level, at the end of 2024 total Assets reached a total of $78.40T,
 up $9.79T since the end of 2023. The increase was based on the growth of investments
 in debt securities, which was the result of the strategies associated with the increase in
 placements by both the parent company and affiliates.
 Regarding Total Liabilities, at the end of 2024 they stood at $72.41T, representing a growth
 of 15.10% compared to the end of 2023, in response to the funding needs of our commercial
 operations. Total consolidated equity at the end of 2024 was $5.98T, up by $297.707B
 compared to the end of 2023.
 Consolidated net income was $481.048B with a growth of 0.31% compared to 2023. The
 increase was mainly based on the growth of Net Other Income, which reached the sum of
 $770.495 B, with a growth of 63.67% compared to the previous year, mainly as a result of
 the net gain by difference in exchange where a year-on-year growth of $213.794 B was
 evidenced. The foregoing, followed by the 4.06% year-on-year variation in Net Interest
 Income and Valuation, equivalent to $90.756B, broken down between Interest Received on
 Credit Portfolio and Leasing Operations and Interest Expense on Deposits.
 There was a variation of -4.54% compared to 2023 of Interest and Similar Expenses, represented
 in $249.412B, mainly explained by the variation in the component of Interest Expense on
 Deposits, which registered a year-on-year variation of -7.36%, as a result of the decrease
 in the volume of fundraising and monetary pressures that do not favor savings, the increase
 compared to the end of 2023 by 6.12% of Financial Obligations is also noteworthy, which
 is equivalent to a variation of $70.297B.
 The Other Net Expenditure item registered an increase of $182.031 B compared to 2023,
 which translates into a variation of 8.91%, in the breakdown of the variation, the increases
 in Personnel Expenditure of 9.42%, Depreciation and Amortization Expense (12.37%) and the
 increase in General Administration Expenses (9.79%) stand out.

 Additionally, as part of our Innovation and Transformation strategy, the commitment of the
 People Digital Transformation Cell was strengthened with the evolutions implemented in
 the digital people engagement tool, with which the participation of digitally onboarded
 customers increased from 77% to 92% at the end of the year. On the other hand, a pilot
 of customer referencing to the fiduciary’s FICs with Metrocuadrado and the digital
 wallet Dale! was initiated, making us the only fiduciary of the group to establish an
 alliance with these two entities. Finally, during 2024, the milestone of being the first
 trust company to allow the digital onboarding of investors to private equity funds in
 the FCP Dalval was achieved.


 On the Digital Transformation of Companies front, the first digital
 onboarding flow was developed for Collective Investment Funds
 for Legal Entities of all segments: Companies 1, Companies
 2, Corporate, Institutional and Government. In this regard, we
 became the first trust company to digitize this process in the
 market.

 Stress Tests
 | SASB FN-CB-550a.2 |

 In the case of the 2024 Stress Tests as regulated in Circular Letter 028 of 2024, four
 scenarios were defined: the Base scenario, which corresponds to a context in which
 the economy and the financial system do not suffer unexpected shocks; an adverse
 scenario, which constitutes a hypothetical context in which the economy and the
 financial system are affected by unexpected shocks which are severe enough to
 produce breaches in the minimum regulatory requirements of solvency and liquidity;
 an adverse scenario with climate risk (rainfall), which adds to the events of the adverse
 scenario, the materialization of acute physical risks derived from climate change; and
 an adverse scenario with mitigating factors, which preserves the macroeconomic
 assumptions of the adverse scenario, but including the mitigating actions carried
 out by the Bank to increase its solvency and liquidity levels above regulatory limits. It
 should be noted that the adverse scenario is totally hypothetical in its construction to
 model non-compliance with the regulatory solvency and CFEN (Net Stable Funding
 Ratio) and is not foreseeable to occur in the medium and long term.
 For this EPR (Stress Test Scheme) exercise that we carried out and in accordance
 with what was defined by SFC (Finance Superintendence of Colombia), it is based
 on information from balance sheet figures at end of December 2023 and is defined
 as the basis for the projections for the following three years: 2024, 2025 and 2026.
 Similarly, 32 variables are considered at the macroeconomic level for each of the
 referred scenarios.
 Regarding the Solvency Ratio, in the base scenario we comply in all the years of the
 projection with the minimum requirements of Basic Solvency, Additional Basic Solvency
 Ratio and Total Solvency Ratio, taking into account the implementation plan of the          As for the CFEN, in the base scenario, the upward behavior of         Additionally, and under the guidance received from the supervisor

 We promote
 sustainable
 businesses
 At Banco de Occidente, we embed environmental, social, and
 governance sustainability at the center of our financial decisions.
 Through our financing strategies, we promote the transition to a
 more sustainable economy, strengthening the competitiveness of
 our clients and generating a positive impact on the environment
 and society.
 With this perspective, we offer financing options that allow our
 clients to incorporate ESG criteria into their economic activities
 and projects. Not only do we have specific lines, such as Occiauto
 Planeta Azul for the acquisition of hybrid and electric vehicles, but,
 in essence, any type of credit within our portfolio can be framed
 as a sustainable solution.

 Wellbeing and Motivation:
 Taking Care of Our People
 At Banco de Occidente, we recognize that the well-being of our employees is key to
 their personal and professional development, as well as to the Bank’s success. For this
 reason, we implement initiatives that promote physical, mental and emotional health,
 creating a work environment where each person can reach their full potential.
 Our programs are designed to positively impact not only employees, but also their
 families, ensuring a work-life balance. Through well-being strategies, we foster a
 culture of motivation, commitment and high performance, contributing to an enriching
 and sustainable work experience.

   Family and Personal
   Life Benefits
                                                          Family Day:
                                                          One day off is granted per semester so that employees can spend time with their
                                                          families. This benefit seeks to strengthen family ties and promote a more cohesive
                                                          work environment. Although there is no exact measurement of usage, leaders
                                                          are encouraged to support their teams in taking advantage of this day.


                                                                                                Maternity Leave:
                                                                                                2 paid days are granted in addition to the maternity leave established by law. This contributes
                                                                                                to the improvement in employees satisfaction and retention, supporting work-life balance.


                                                          Paternity Leave:
                                                          Similarly, 2 paid days are granted in addition to the paternity leave established by
                                                          law, encouraging active participation of fathers in the first days of their children’s lives.


                                                                                                    Bereavement leave:
                                                                                                    In the event of the death of a close relative, additional paid days are granted according to the
                                                                                                    relationship (first degree of consanguinity: 1 additional day; second degree: leave established
                                                                                                    by law). This benefit seeks to provide emotional support and allow adequate time for mourning.


                                                          Birthday afternoon:
                                                          Each employees can take a paid half working day on their birthday, choosing
                                                          between morning or afternoon. This benefit promotes the well-being of
                                                          employees, allowing them to enjoy personal time on a meaningful date.

                                                                 Diversity, Equity,
                                                                 and Inclusion
                                                                 SDG 8.5; 10.2


                                                                 At Banco de Occidente we have a common purpose and we know that to achieve it we have a
                                                                 team that reflects our values and corporate identity. Respect, as the main value of our culture, is
                                                                 transversal to all our operations and reaffirms our commitment to the protection of human rights
                                                                 and the creation of diverse environments, free of discrimination, violence and harassment in
                                                                 the workplace. We guarantee the physical, mental and social well-being of our employees and
                                                                 stakeholders, in line with our Human Rights Policy, Internal Work Regulations and Code of Ethics
                                                                 and Conduct.
                                                                 Currently, we are part of Asobancaria’s Social Protocol, a voluntary agreement that promotes
                                                                 equity, diversity and inclusion in the Colombian financial sector. This protocol establishes good
                                                                 practices in four key strategies: internal culture, financial education and inclusion, value proposition
                                                                 and financial risk management.
                                                                 Likewise, under our Human Rights Due Diligence approach, we incorporate diversity, equity and
                                                                 inclusion criteria in the Human Rights Policy, aligned with the United Nations Guiding Principles,
                                                                 as well as in the Code of Ethics and Conduct and the Internal Work Regulations. Our 2024 was
                                                                 focused on:

Acknowledgements
                     At Banco de Occidente, we are convinced that sustainability is a
                     collective effort and that true impact is built with the participation
                     of everyone. This report is a reflection of the commitment of those
                     who, from different fronts, have contributed to strengthening our
                     vision of responsible and sustainable business.

                   To our employees, thank you for your dedication and for making sustainability an essential part
                   of our day-to-day work. To our customers and allies, for trusting us and motivating us to continue
                   innovating in solutions that generate shared value. To our communities, for allowing us to be part
                   of their growth and development, and to our investors and other stakeholders, for accompanying
                   us on this path and reaffirming with us the importance of integrating environmental, social and
                   governance criteria in our management.
                   From the Sustainability Management, we reaffirm our commitment to continue working on the side
                   of those who do, moving forward with determination in the construction of a more sustainable,
                   equitable and prosperous future for all. Let’s continue building together.

                                                         Chapter on Responsible Growth and Comprehensive Risk Management; Financial outlook and stock market performance.
                                                         Change in the ROI Methodology: to ensure compliance with the requirements of the Dow Jones
                                                         Sustainability Index (DJSI), we made an update to the formula used to calculate the Return on
                                                         Investment in Human Capital (HC-ROI). In this new methodology, we make sure to:
                                                         Total income: includes the total income received by the company before making any
                                                         deductions, including interest and valuation income, income from commissions and fees, net
                                                         income from financial assets or liabilities held for trading, and other net income.
                                                         Total operating expenses: are reported in line with accepted accounting and financial reporting standards,
                                                         including general administrative expenses, depreciation and amortization expenses, personnel expenses,
                                                         interest and similar expenses, commission and fee expenses, and other operating expenses.
                      201-1 Direct Economic Value        Total employees-related expenses: Considers all labor costs, including salaries,                                                            Financial stability and
    64       GRI                                                                                                                                                                         x
                      Generated and Distributed          benefits, training programs, pensions, and severance payments.                                                                              profitable growth
                                                         Given this adjustment in the methodology, the historical data have been recalculated, which
                                                         has generated changes in the previously reported values. HC ROI result recalculated for the last
                                                         five years is as follows: 2020: 30.208; 2021: 3.99; 2022: 3.43; 2023: 3.65; 2024: 3.91.
                                                         It is observed that in 2020 there was a significantly high value compared to the following years. This was related to
                                                         extraordinary factors, such as financial optimization strategies, impacts derived from the pandemic and/or structural
                                                         changes in the bank. From 2021 onwards, the HC ROI stabilizes in a more consistent range, with a decline in 2022 (3.43)
                                                         and a gradual recovery in subsequent years (3.65 in 2023 and 3.91 in 2024). This behavior demonstrates a positive
                                                         trend in the efficiency of the use of human capital, which we highlight for improvements in productivity, optimization
                                                         of labor costs and the strengthening of human talent strategies. This analysis allows us to have a clearer view of the
                                                         impact of human capital on the bank’s profitability, ensuring alignment with international sustainability standards.

                      Safety Management System


                                                           At Banco de Occidente, we carry out a detailed analysis to identify the risks present in all areas of the
                                                           organization, including occupational health and safety issues and environmental care. This process allows
                                                           us to recognize potential threats and apply proactive measures to reduce their impact. Next, we carry out
                      403-2 Hazard Identification,
                                                           a comprehensive risk assessment, where we examine both the probability of occurrence and the possible
    179      GRI      Risk Assessment, and                                                                                                                                                         Labor relations
                                                           consequences of each identified risk. With this information, we set priorities and design specific strategies
                      Incident Investigation
                                                           to manage them effectively. In the event of an incident, we conduct a thorough investigation to identify the
                                                           root causes and implement improvements that optimize our processes and procedures. We focus on avoiding
                                                           the repetition of similar events and continuously strengthening our culture of safety and sustainability.

                                                       At Banco de Occidente, we are constantly striving to promote safe and healthy practices. The safety and health
                                                       of all employees, regardless of their type of employment relationship with the organization, is a priority for us.
                                                       To ensure the uniform application of these principles throughout our value chain, we have developed robust
                      403-4 Employeese
                                                       monitoring and evaluation mechanisms. Our employees also actively participate in the Occupational Health
                      Engagement, Consultation,
    179      GRI                                       and Safety Management System (OH&S-MS). In Colombia, we have the COPASST (Joint Committee on Safety                                          Labor relations
                      and Communication on
                                                       and Health at Work). This committee is formed in accordance with local regulations, guaranteeing the equitable
                      Occupational Health and Safety
                                                       representation of employer and employees, and meets monthly to address occupational safety issues, organize
                                                       training, carry out safety inspections and lead prevention campaigns. Likewise, we continuously monitor key health
                                                       and safety indicators, promoting a constant improvement of working conditions throughout our operation.


                      403-5 Occupational Health and
    179      GRI                                       Chapter Empowering People and Communities; Occupational Health and Safety.                                                                   Labor relations
                      Safety Training of Employees

                                                       From the Occupational Medicine Program, we have implemented a series of initiatives designed to
                                                       promote the comprehensive well-being of our employees, focusing on both physical and mental health
                                                       care. These activities seek to generate healthy habits that contribute to a more balanced life, thus
                                                       improving their quality of life and work performance. Every year we carry out Health Week, an event
                                                       that includes a series of activities focused on the promotion of healthy habits. Activities include:
                                                       • Nutrition and healthy eating: workshops and advice on balanced eating.
                                                       • Promotion of physical activity: group classes and recommendations for an active life.
                                                       • Emotional well-being: talks and workshops on stress management, resilience and mental health.
                                                       • Disease prevention: vaccination days and medical check-ups.
                                                       • Trends in safety and occupational risks: training in ergonomics and risk prevention.
                      403-6 Employees
    179      GRI                                       This event takes place at our administrative headquarters nationwide and is complemented                                                     Labor relations
                      Health Promotion
                                                       by virtual activities to ensure the participation of employees in regional offices.
                                                       Recreational and cultural activities: throughout the year, we promote physical activity and emotional well-being through
                                                       various recreational and cultural activities, coordinated by our work environment team. Some of these include:
                                                       • Sports tournaments: beach volleyball competitions and corporate marathons.
                                                       • Cultural and social activities: ecological walks, film screenings and volunteer
                                                       days to involve employees in social and environmental actions.
                                                       In addition, we have established agreements with various sports institutions, such as gyms
                                                       and wellness centers, to offer our employees access to facilities and programs that allow
                                                       them to maintain a regular exercise routine and improve their quality of life.

                                                                3. TCFD Report

                                                                TCFD
                                                                Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures
                                                                Climate change represents one of the most significant challenges of our time, and at Banco de Occidente
                                                                we are committed to playing an active role in mitigating it. This report, prepared in accordance with the
                                                                recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD), reflects our dedication to
                                                                transparency and climate-related risk management. In this sense, we have developed a sustainability strategy
                                                                that seeks to impact society, protect the environment and promote social development in the territories in
                                                                which we operate.
                                                                The TCFD Initiative is a framework of recommendations designed to promote the disclosure of climate-related
                                                                financial information. It seeks to offer solid guidelines that allow companies to communicate more effectively
                                                                the financial risks associated with climate change.
                                                                In 2022, we began our roadmap for the adoption of the TCFD framework, also aligning with the instructions
                                                                of the External Circular No. 031 of 2021 of the Finance Superintendence of Colombia (SFC). This process has
                                                                involved different levels and areas of Banco de Occidente, allowing us to address each of the four pillars
                                                                and eleven recommendations of the TCFD framework.
                                                                As a financial institution committed to the fight against climate change and in compliance with Colombian
                                                                legislation, we have adhered to this framework, preparing our first TCFD report in 2023. This adhesion
                                                                reinforces our commitment to transparency and management of climate-related financial risks, aligning us
                                                                with international best practices.
                                                                At Banco de Occidente, we understand that the fight against climate change requires a collective and
                                                                continuous effort. We are committed to continuing to work to promote sustainable practices and protect
                                                                our planet for future generations.
                                                                .

 Internal policies
 and frameworks
 Environmental and Climate Change Policy of
 Banco de Occidente and Affiliates: In our policy we
 establish the general principles that we must follow
 to align and develop initiatives that respond to the
 commitments of the sustainability strategy, in such a
 way that they are oriented to the management of the
 business around economic, social, environmental and
 corporate governance matters. For us, it is essential
 to consolidate sustainability and its articulation with
 the purpose and business model of the Bank and its
 affiliates. With this policy, we want to strengthen the
 processes for the improvement of business operations,
 organizational reputation and the positioning of the
 organization and its affiliates as a benchmark in the
 Colombian financial sector.

 Physical risks:                                        Distribution of physical risks assessed by time horizon
 These are those risks related to extreme weather
 events. These can be acute or chronic.                     Short-term                   Medium-term                    Long-term
     Acute: Refers to a specific disaster or increase         < 1 year                   Up to 3 years               More than 4 years
     in extreme and/or fast-onset weather events
     such as torrential floods, landslides, cyclones,
     floods, and heat waves.
     Chronic: Long-term changes in weather
     patterns, such as changes in precipitation
     regimes and extreme variability in weather
     patterns, increase in the average temperature                 25%                           50%                               25%
     of the region, and rising sea levels.
